newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa June new car sales up 4.3 percent y/y.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa June new car sales up 4.3 percent y/y.

text.p: New car sales rose 4.3 percent year-on-year and 4.2 percent month-on-month to 20,191 units in June, the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (Naamsa) said on Thursday.

"Following the sharp year-on-year decline in sales in May...the new car market benefitted from aggressive marketing strategies by various manufacturers and continued interest in new models," the association said in a statement.
New car sales slumped 21.2 percent year-on-year in May and rose just 0.7 percent month-on-month.

Naamsa noted, however, that growth in medium commercial vehicle sales had slowed considerably, while sales of heavy commercial vehicles had been extremely weak -- the latter suggesting a substantial slowdown in fixed investment growth.
Medium commercial vehicle sales rose 6.5 percent year-on-year, but fell 15.2 percent month-on-month. Heavy vehicle sales were down 25.1 percent year-on-year and 4.3 percent month-on-month.

It said that against the background of high real interest rates and consumer indebtedness, a subdued economic environment and with government spending likely to decline in the months ahead, new vehicle sales would remain under pressure over the remainder of the year.
New car sales would also be negatively affected by the "fairly punitive" increases in fringe benefit taxes on the use of company cars as well as in the case of car allownaces, it added.

Toyota 8,912, Samcor 5,032, Delta 4,969, Volkswagen 4,417, Nissan 3,321, Mercedes-Benz 2,392, BMW 1,098, Daewoo 533, Land Rover SA 276, Chrysler 162, Iveco 76, MAN 58, Tyco 49, Freightliner 21, ERF 16, Scania 9, Subaru 7, AAD 4.
